CausalChain: Tumor Cells -> Secretion of heterogeneous EV populations (one enriched in miR-21, miR-155, IL-6, GM-CSF; another carrying miR-126) -> Preferential uptake of the miR-21/miR-155/cytokine EV subpopulation by mature myeloid cells -> Downregulation of IRF-8 and C/EBPα -> Skewed differentiation toward immunosuppressive MDSCs -> Enhanced T cell inhibition and tumor immune escape
Hypothesis: Building on established evidence that tumor-derived EVs mediate diverse aspects of cancer progression, we propose that a specific subpopulation of EVs, enriched with miR-21, miR-155, IL-6, and GM-CSF, plays a decisive role in modulating the immune microenvironment. Upon uptake by mature myeloid cells, these EVs trigger a downregulation of the transcription factors IRF-8 and C/EBPα, crucial for proper myeloid differentiation, thereby promoting the formation of immunosuppressive MDSCs. This targeted reprogramming of myeloid cells contributes to a more effective T cell inhibition and promotes tumor immune escape. Our approach distinguishes this mechanistic pathway from other EV functions (e.g., those mediated by miR-126 affecting tumor cell migration) by employing single-cell RNA sequencing to delineate cell-type specific responses, CRISPR-based screens to elucidate the role of individual molecular actors, and nanotechnology to isolate and manipulate the relevant EV subpopulations. By temporally profiling EV uptake and employing precise quantitative measurements, we aim to validate the kinetics and stoichiometric requirements of this dual-cargo delivery system, which represents a promising target for innovative cancer immunotherapy strategies.
Abstract: We hypothesize that tumor cells secrete heterogeneous populations of extracellular vesicles (EVs), wherein a distinct subpopulation is enriched in the oncogenic miRNAs miR-21 and miR-155 along with cytokine modulators such as IL-6 and GM-CSF. This specialized EV fraction is preferentially taken up by mature myeloid cells in the tumor microenvironment, where the cargo—acting in concert—downregulates critical transcription factors IRF-8 and C/EBPα. This shift in transcriptional regulation subsequently skews myeloid differentiation toward the generation of immunosuppressive myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs), thereby enhancing T cell inhibition and facilitating tumor immune evasion. In parallel, other EV subpopulations carrying miR-126 and similar molecules modulate tumor cell migration and invasion. To dissect these overlapping roles, we propose a multi-pronged experimental strategy that leverages advanced single-cell RNA sequencing to resolve cellular heterogeneity, CRISPR-based functional screens to quantify the contribution of each cargo element, and time-course, dose-response analyses to map the kinetics of EV uptake and downstream signaling. Moreover, we will explore nanotechnology-driven approaches to both isolate and engineer specific EV subpopulations and employ miRNA antagonists as a therapeutic intervention to disrupt the pro-tumorigenic reprogramming of immune cells.
Orignal_vs_New: The revised hypothesis retains the original concept that tumor-derived EVs deliver a cocktail of oncogenic miRNAs (miR-21 and miR-155) and cytokine modulators (IL-6, GM-CSF) leading to downregulation of IRF-8 and C/EBPα and subsequent MDSC formation. However, it now incorporates a dual-faceted view by recognizing the heterogeneity of EV populations and explicitly differentiates the miR-21/miR-155 axis from other EV-mediated miRNA effects (such as those involving miR-126). The new hypothesis addresses reviewer concerns by: (1) emphasizing the need for quantitative and temporal dynamics of EV cargo delivery; (2) outlining the use of advanced techniques (single-cell RNA sequencing, CRISPR screens, and nanotechnology-based EV engineering) to disentangle the specific contributions of each cargo type; and (3) explicitly incorporating mechanistic details of EV uptake and the subsequent transcriptional reprogramming of myeloid cells. This comprehensive framework not only aligns with observed evidence but also enhances the practical implementability of the proposed therapeutic strategies.
